upstream.notes:
SPLIT INTO TWO PRs. AGENTS.md closes bundled PRs ("One problem per PR"), so the working tree holds two disjoint file sets. PR 1 (pr-body.md, title above) is the three context changes: SKILL.md, the three SDD templates, code-reviewer.md, requesting-code-review/SKILL.md. PR 2 (/home/longman/.claude/reviews/2026-09-21-1305-app-subagent-apply/upstream/pr-body-task-brief.md, title "fix(sdd): end a task brief at the next plan-level section") is scripts/task-brief plus tests/claude-code/test-sdd-workspace.sh. Splitting is `git add` by path.

TEST OUTPUT. `bash tests/claude-code/test-sdd-workspace.sh` passes, 27 assertions including 3 new ones (full verbatim output is in summary.md): "[PASS] task-brief stops the last task at the next plan-level section", "[PASS] task-brief keeps a task's deeper sub-headings and stops at the next task", "[PASS] task-brief does not cut a task on a heading inside ambiguous fencing", final line "PASS", exit 0. `bash tests/claude-code/test-worktree-path-policy.sh` prints "STATUS: PASSED"; `bash tests/claude-code/test-executing-plans-scripts.sh` prints "PASS". Not run: tests/claude-code/test-subagent-driven-development.sh (the fourth file in run-skill-tests.sh), which drives the installed plugin through the claude CLI over nine prompts and asserts on how an agent describes the skill; scripts/lint-shell.sh could not run because shellcheck is not installed here ("error: required tool 'shellcheck' is not on PATH"), so `bash -n` was used on both shell files and passes.

DECISIONS YOU SHOULD OVERRULE IF YOU DISAGREE, THREE OF THEM:

1. #1966 is a partial duplicate of item 1 and AGENTS.md says to stop and tell you when duplicates exist. I did not drop item 1, because #1966 covers only the task reviewer (its author deferred the re-reviewer and code-reviewer.md), and the fix loop cannot send "a file path plus ids" unless the reviewer writes a file with ids in it. The PR body says this outright and offers the maintainer the smaller path (land #1966, reduce this PR to the re-review, the final review and the ids). If you would rather not risk the duplicate charge, the alternative is to open only the re-review and code-reviewer parts as a follow-up to #1966.

2. The PR bodies fill the mandatory "Who is submitting this PR?" disclosure table with the model, harness version and plugin list. That contradicts your rules/git.md line "Never mention Claude Code in PR or MR descriptions", but AGENTS.md closes contributions that hide their authoring environment, and the table is a required section. Delete the table if you prefer your rule; the PR will then be closed on disclosure grounds.

3. Em dashes: my added sentences use none. Dashes remain in three places I did not author fresh: lines whose surrounding sentence already had one and that I extended in place (Continuous execution, Reviewer inputs, the "Rounds 1-3 —" bold lead that its "Rounds 4-5 —" sibling matches), and the "- `[NAME]` — description" separator used by every entry of the templates' placeholder lists. Say the word and I will purge those too, at the cost of visible inconsistency with the neighbouring lines.

WHAT I CHANGED MID-COURSE, AND WHY IT MATTERS. The prepared awk in scripts-minimal/task-brief ends a task at the next same-or-shallower heading. Applied to obra/superpowers' own plans it truncates real task content: 2026-04-06-worktree-rototill.md task 2 went 261 lines to 60 and 2026-08-27-diagnosing-superpowers.md task 4 went 305 to 43, because those tasks embed whole markdown documents whose inner bare ``` closes the outer fence under CommonMark. The fix that shipped here gates the new terminator on two fence parses agreeing the heading is outside a fence (the existing toggle, plus a CommonMark parse added under its own name so #2304 still merges), and leaves the existing Task-heading detection byte-identical. Re-measured after the change: 93 real plans on this machine, 732 task extractions, 78 change, 847 lines removed, none grows, and the first line dropped is a plan-level heading in every case (## Self-review notes 7, ## Self-Review 6, ## Self-review 5, ## Done when 5, ## Final verification 3, then ## Spec coverage check, ## Notes for the reviewer, ## Chunk 2, ## Amendment 1..4). On the repository's own 16 plans, 13 task extractions improve and none truncates.

THE WEAK POINT OF PR 1. AGENTS.md requires eval evidence for skill-content changes ("Skills are not prose, they are code"). There is none after the change: all five runs measured are pre-change, and the Evaluation and Rigor sections say so plainly rather than dressing arithmetic up as an eval. Expect the maintainers to ask for an A/B, and expect that to be the most likely rejection ground. If you want it, the cheapest version is two reviewer subagents on one seeded-flaw diff, current prompt versus new prompt, counting detection parity and final-message size, which is exactly the shape #1966 ran and reported.

ACCURACY FIXES I MADE TO THE SOURCE CLAIMS: the brief's "one unit consumed 19 percent of the iac subagent total" covers the implementer plus its six re-reviews, so the skill text says "the one task whose implementer was resumed to 683k tokens", not "one implementer". The re-review share of review characters is 29 to 50 percent across the three long runs (49.8, 38.4, 28.9), not a tighter band.

Nothing was committed, no branch was created or switched (still on main at 5bf4e78), nothing was pushed, and no PR was opened. Note that AGENTS.md requires PRs to target `dev`, not `main`.
